summary: Reserves an IPv6 unicast address prefix for use in examples in RFCs, books and other documentation. Using it avoids conflicts with real networks, and avoids site-local or link-local addresses, which have special meanings.

eli5.summary: Writers of books use a pretend address that nobody really lives at, so no real house gets mail by mistake. This document picks the pretend IPv6 address.

questions: what ipv6 address should i use in examples
subtitle: The IPv6 prefix 2001:DB8::/32, set aside so examples never point at real networks.

tldr.problem: IPv6 documentation used address prefixes from real organizations or unallocated space, which risks conflicts with real allocations and with production systems.
tldr.mechanism: The memo reserves the unicast prefix 2001:DB8::/32, allocated by APNIC, for examples in RFCs, books and documentation.
tldr.outcome: Operators should treat the prefix as non-routeable and may add it to packet filters. It is updated by RFC 9637.

today: RFC 3849 is an Informational memo that is updated by RFC 9637.

sections.title: Why a Documentation Prefix
sections.content:
The IPv6 address architecture did not allocate a prefix for documentation. Examples were drawn from blocks already held by organizations or ISPs, or from the unallocated pool, which conflicts with current or future allocations.

The same problem was already seen with IPv4, where literal use of documented examples in production caused address and routing conflicts. Some top level DNS names were reserved for the same purpose in RFC 2606.
sections.eli5: If a book uses a real address, readers who copy it may disturb a real family. A pretend address avoids that.

sections.title: The Prefix
sections.content:
Site-local and link-local addresses have special meaning in IPv6, so they cannot be used in many examples; a unicast block is required. After a proposal was accepted in the Asia Pacific addressing community, APNIC allocated a prefix within a conventional allocation size so that documentation can match real deployments.

The prefix is 2001:DB8::/32. It can also be used to generate multicast addresses for documentation using the unicast prefix-based proposal, but other kinds of multicast addresses are out of scope.
sections.eli5: One reserved block of numbers is for pretend examples only, and the same block can help make pretend group addresses.

sections.title: Operational Implications
sections.content: Network operators should add this prefix to the list of non-routeable IPv6 address space, and to packet filters if they are deployed. It is not a local-use prefix, so filters may be used in both local and public contexts.
sections.eli5: Network keepers should make sure pretend addresses never travel on the real network.

sections.title: IANA and Security
sections.content: IANA is to record 2001:DB8::/32 as a documentation-only prefix in the IPv6 address registry, and no end party is to be assigned it. The memo says IPv6 addressing documents have no direct impact on Internet infrastructure security.
sections.eli5: The registry writes down that this block is just for pretend, and nobody may own it.

references.text: Hinden, R. and S. Deering, "Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6) Addressing Architecture", RFC 3513, April 2003.

Haberman, B. and D. Thaler, "Unicast-Prefix-based IPv6 Multicast Addresses", RFC 3306, August 2002.
